title: Resonance and Q
blurb: Find a circuit's resonant frequency, say what series and parallel circuits do there, and use Q to get bandwidth.

E5A01.why: At resonance XL and XC are equal and cancel, so only R limits current. Each reactance's voltage is **Q** times the source voltage, which can be far larger.
E5A01.trap: Low Q gives little voltage gain. Capacitance or resistance alone do not multiply voltage.

E5A02.trap: 22.36 is 1 ÷ √(LC), which is in rad/s. Divide by 2π for hertz.

E5A03.why: At series resonance XL cancels XC, leaving only resistance: Z ≈ **R**, the minimum.
E5A03.trap: XL and XC are each large but cancel, so they do not set Z.

E5A04.why: At parallel resonance the L and C branches cancel, leaving the resistor: Z ≈ **R**, the maximum.
E5A04.trap: Parallel is the opposite of series: impedance peaks here, it doesn't dip.

E5A05.why: BW = f₀ ÷ Q, so raising Q **narrows** the bandwidth of the matching circuit.

E5A06.why: In a parallel LC circuit at resonance, energy swings between L and C. The **circulating current is maximum** while the line current is minimum.
E5A06.trap: The line current is the minimum; the loop current inside is the maximum.

E5A07.why: Parallel resonance is highest impedance, so the source supplies the **minimum** current.
E5A07.trap: Maximum current is the series case.

E5A08.why: At resonance net reactance is zero, so the circuit looks purely resistive: voltage and current are **in phase**.

E5A09.why: Parallel Q = R ÷ X. A larger parallel R means less loss, so higher Q.
E5A09.trap: X ÷ R is the series formula; parallel is inverted.

E5A10.trap: Watch the prefix: 7.12 kHz and 23.5 MHz are the wrong scale or unit.

E5A11.trap: 23.67 kHz is half of it. BW is the full width between the half-power points.

E5A13.why: Voltage across L or C is Q times the source voltage, so raising Q makes **internal voltages** increase.
